process_observations.observation: The step's acceptance_tests[0] description predicted the checker's exact output before the artefact existed - score 95, one SharingRules WARN, 0 blocking, exit 0 - and the run matched it line for line. A test description that names the expected non-zero-severity finding is what stopped a correct artefact reading as a failure.

Every fact the manifest needed was already written down somewhere in the build - the version decision in the milestone:M3 gate note, the Apex exception in the contract, the blocked reasons on the two blocked steps, the ordering hazards collated by M5-S04. This step was a join across existing records rather than a new decision, which is the shape the last step of a build should have.

The step-tester's always-on manifest check reads the step's OWN artefact directory in both directions, and this step's directory holds only package.xml and deploy-order.md while its 56 members' files live under sixteen sibling step directories. Read literally, every member is a member-without-a-file. The step's acceptance_tests[2] describes the whole-tree reading the check actually needs; nothing in agents/step-tester/AGENT.md Step 3 carves out the build-level manifest the way rule 1 carves out the apex-builder step.

This run claimed the step running after the owning agent's reads and writes rather than before them, which inverts build-step-runner Step 3's ordering. Nothing was lost - the step was pending, in next, and un-gated throughout, and the claim was written before the terminal transition - but a crash between the first write and the claim would have left artefacts on disk under a step still reading pending. Recorded rather than glossed.

set-status ... running printed three unrelated WARNs about non-standard checker argument forms on M5-S02 and M5-S04 before doing its own work. They are the documented library backlog in standards/build-orchestration.md section 5 and not about this step, but they arrive on every plan write and are easy to read as this step's problem.

M5 now has one step left un-run (M5-S02, blocked) and one gate pending. The M5 milestone's manual acceptance lines on this step - W12 1 through 3 of 3 - cannot be ticked by any agent, and two of them assert properties of the two files this step just wrote, so the gate reader has to open both files rather than read a verdict.
